text: Harness: cross-model verifier stage returning verified, failed or unverifiable
description: After execute, the verifier role (a different model family than the executor) gets only: idea text + acceptance evidence, the diff, the commands the executor claims to have run. It may re-run the tests itself (read-only + test commands). Returns verified | failed | unverifiable with reasons. Harness maps: verified -> implemented with the verdict in the status comment; failed -> back to open with the objection; unverifiable -> review for Felix. Pluggable so external verifiers (recompute-kit, ThoughtProof) can be a backend later.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: A verifier built by someone else is independent by construction and makes 'verified' claims credible to outside users.

Receipts from commands the harness ran itself make 'verified' depend on observed exit codes, not on the executor's or verifier's word; refuted if, in the traces, receipts never change a verdict the verifier model would have given anyway.
supportingConnections.reflection: Unclear yet: the mechanism works in tests, but whether receipts change real verdicts can only be read from traces of real-model cycles.

status.comment: Done: verify stage sees only idea, executor summary, claimed evidence and commands, git status and diff; read-only code tools + run_command; verified->implemented (evidence + reasons), failed->open with the objection, unverifiable->review; a missing verdict counts as unverifiable. A different model family is now configurable via loops.json roles.verifier (e6bd3fd6), and the worker warns when it equals the executor. Missing: a pluggable external verifier backend (recompute-kit, ThoughtProof; see 43166d16 and the meetings on 13 and 17 Nov).
